A1.y: Red, blue and green are colours. Apple is a fruit.
Cat, dog and cow are animals. A chair is furniture.
One, two and three are numbers. Blue is a colour.
Apple, banana and orange are fruit. A carrot is a vegetable.
Monday, Friday and Sunday are days of the week. June is a month.
Mother, father and sister are family members. A teacher works at a school.
Hand, foot and nose are parts of the body. A shoe is clothing.
Milk, water and juice are drinks. Bread is food you eat.
Shirt, dress and coat are clothes. A spoon is for eating.
January, March and July are months. Tuesday is a day of the week.
Carrot, potato and onion are vegetables. A banana is a fruit.
Car, bus and train are transport. A tree is a plant.
Knife, fork and spoon are for eating. A sock is clothing.
Circle, square and triangle are shapes. Purple is a colour.
Pen, pencil and ruler are school things. A pillow is for your bed.
Bed, table and chair are furniture. A cup is for drinking.
Sunny, rainy and windy describe the weather. Hungry describes how you feel.
Kitchen, bedroom and bathroom are rooms in a house. A garden is outside.
Eagle, parrot and owl are birds. A dolphin lives in the sea.
Doctor, nurse and cook are jobs. Sister is a family word.
Spring, summer and winter are seasons. Morning is a time of day.
Football, tennis and golf are sports. A piano is a musical instrument.
Piano, guitar and drum are musical instruments. A hammer is a tool.
Happy, sad and angry are feelings. Tall describes how big someone is.
Cow, sheep and pig live on a farm. A lion is a wild animal.
Lion, tiger and zebra are wild animals. A hen lives on a farm.
Fish, shark and whale live in the sea. A horse lives on land.
Breakfast, lunch and dinner are meals. A kitchen is a room.
Eyes, mouth and ears are on your face. Knees are on your legs.
Run, jump and swim are actions. A table is a thing.
Doll, ball and kite are toys. Soup is food.
Bank, school and hospital are buildings. A cloud is in the sky.
Cake, candy and chocolate are sweet. Salt is not sweet.
Bee, ant and butterfly are insects. A frog is not an insect.
Tree, flower and grass are plants. A stone is not alive.
Pink, brown and grey are colours. Round is a shape word.
First, second and third show order. Three is a number for counting.
Grandma, grandpa and uncle are family. A neighbour lives near you.
Shoes, boots and sandals go on your feet. Gloves go on your hands.
Tea, coffee and hot chocolate are hot drinks. Lemonade is a cold drink.
What, where and when are question words. Because gives a reason.
In, on and under tell you where something is. Jump is an action.
Sun, moon and stars are in the sky. Grass is on the ground.
Fridge, oven and microwave are in the kitchen. A sofa is in the living room.
Sweet, salty and sour are tastes. Loud describes a sound.
Soap, towel and toothbrush are bathroom things. A pillow is for the bed.
Grape, cherry and lemon are fruit. Rice is a grain.
Phone, laptop and television are electronic. A blanket is not.
House, flat and apartment are homes. An office is a place of work.
Big, small and long describe size. Green is a colour.

A2.y: Big, large and huge mean not small. Tiny means very small.
Sad, unhappy and upset mean feeling bad. Glad means happy.
Fast, quick and speedy mean moving with speed. Slow is the opposite.
Love, like and enjoy are positive feelings. Hate is a strong negative feeling.
Easy, simple and basic mean not hard. Difficult means hard.
Wet, damp and soaked describe water on something. Dry means no water.
Finish, end and stop mean something is over. Begin means start.
Tired, sleepy and exhausted mean you need rest. Energetic means full of energy.
Dirty, messy and untidy mean not in order. Neat means clean and tidy.
Rich, wealthy and well-off mean having lots of money. Poor means having little.
Old, ancient and elderly mean having lived a long time. Young is the opposite.
Loud, noisy and deafening mean making lots of sound. Quiet means little sound.
Kind, friendly and helpful are good qualities. Rude is a bad quality.
Lazy, rude and selfish are negative qualities. Generous is a positive quality.
At a bakery, pharmacy and bookshop you buy things. At a library you borrow books.
Doctors, nurses and surgeons work in hospitals. A pilot flies planes.
Menu, waiter and bill are restaurant words. A patient is in a hospital.
Headache, cough and fever are signs of illness. A holiday is time off.
Snow, ice and frost come with cold weather. Sunshine is warm and bright.
Cloudy, foggy and stormy describe grey, dark weather. Sunny describes bright weather.
Cash, coin and banknote are money. A receipt is paper showing what you paid.
Runway, gate and check-in are at an airport. A platform is at a train station.
Painting, reading and dancing are hobbies. Ironing is housework.
Tidy, sweep and dust are housework. Sunbathe means relax in the sun.
Jazz, rock and pop are music styles. Ballet is a type of dance.
Tennis, golf and basketball use a ball. Swimming does not.
Surfing, sailing and diving happen on or in water. Skiing happens on snow.
Bottle, jar and can hold things inside. A spoon is for eating.
Wood, glass and metal are materials. A circle is a shape.
Minute, hour and second measure time. A metre measures length.
Metre, kilometre and centimetre measure length. A kilogram measures weight.
North, south and west are compass directions. Middle means the centre.
Blond, curly and straight describe hair. Slim describes a body.
Boat, ship and ferry travel on water. A truck travels on roads.
Plane, helicopter and jet fly in the air. A submarine goes under water.
Cousin, aunt and nephew are relatives. A colleague is someone you work with.
Office, factory and warehouse are places of work. A playground is for children to play.
Boil, fry and bake are ways of cooking. Sew means make clothes with a needle.
Pen, marker and crayon are for writing or drawing. An eraser removes marks.
Ring, necklace and bracelet are jewellery. A belt is clothing.
Birthday, wedding and party are celebrations. An exam is a test.
Hammer, saw and screwdriver are tools. A towel is for drying.
Tent, campfire and sleeping bag are for camping. A dishwasher is a kitchen machine.
Price, discount and sale are shopping words. A passport is for travel.
Arrive, come and enter mean getting to a place. Leave means going away.
Receive, get and accept mean something comes to you. Give means you hand it to someone.
Smile, laugh and grin show you are happy. Cry usually shows you are sad.
Run, rush and hurry mean moving fast. Stroll means walking slowly.
Shout, scream and yell mean speaking very loudly. Whisper means speaking very quietly.
Look, watch and stare use your eyes. Listen uses your ears.

B1.y: We make a mistake, a decision and a noise. But we do homework.
We do the dishes, shopping and laundry. But we make the bed.
We take a photo, a shower and a break. But we make a promise.
You catch a bus, a cold and a fish. You make a decision.
Clever, smart and intelligent mean quick to learn. Foolish means silly.
Brave, bold and fearless mean not afraid. Cowardly means easily afraid.
Angry, cross and annoyed mean not pleased. Calm means peaceful and relaxed.
Afraid, frightened and terrified mean full of fear. Relaxed means calm.
Strange, odd and weird mean unusual. Normal means usual.
Polite, courteous and respectful mean good manners. Rude means bad manners.
Ill, sick and unwell mean not feeling well. Healthy means well.
Enormous, gigantic and massive mean very big. Miniature means very small.
Famous, well-known and celebrated mean many people know you. Unknown means nobody does.
Honest, truthful and sincere mean telling the truth. Dishonest means lying.
Delicious, tasty and yummy mean food tastes good. Disgusting means it tastes bad.
Expensive, costly and pricey mean it costs a lot. Affordable means you can pay for it.
Mean, stingy and tight-fisted mean not liking to give. Generous means happy to give.
Rise, grow and increase mean go up. Fall means go down.
Freezing, chilly and cool describe cold temperatures. Boiling means very hot.
Shy, timid and quiet describe people who avoid attention. Outgoing means sociable.
Cheerful, positive and optimistic mean expecting good things. Pessimistic means expecting bad things.
Job, career and profession are work you are paid for. A hobby is for fun.
Trip, journey and voyage mean travelling. A destination is the place you travel to.
Salary, wage and income are money you receive. A bill is money you must pay.
We say heavy rain, heavy traffic and heavy smoker. But we say bright sunshine.
We say strong coffee, strong wind and strong opinion. But we say heavy rain.
We say fast food, fast car and fast train. But we say a quick glance.
We pay attention, pay a visit and pay a compliment. But we give a speech.
We keep a secret, a promise and calm. But we take a shower.
We break a record, a promise and the law. But we make the bed.
We go shopping, fishing and camping. But we do the cooking.
Give up, quit and stop mean not continue. Carry on means continue.
Degree, diploma and certificate are qualifications you receive. An exam is a test.
Lecturer, professor and tutor teach students. A landlord rents out homes.
Burglar, thief and robber are criminals who steal. A judge works in a court.
Pollution, litter and smog harm the environment. Recycling helps it.
Brake, gear and steering wheel are car parts. A propeller moves planes and boats.
Chew, swallow and bite are things you do with your mouth. Sniff uses your nose.
Stroll, wander and march are ways of walking. Sprint means run very fast.
Giggle, chuckle and laugh show amusement. Sob means cry loudly.
Glance, peek and gaze are ways of looking. Overhear is about hearing.
Grab, grip and hold mean keep something in your hand. Release means let it go.
Agree, accept and approve mean saying yes. Refuse means saying no.
Allow, let and permit mean say yes to something. Forbid means say no.
Damage, harm and ruin mean make something worse. Repair means fix it.
We say afraid of, proud of and fond of. But we say interested in.
We say good at, bad at and excellent at. But we say keen on.
Teacher, actor and driver are people. Movement is an action, not a person.
Quickly, slowly and carefully are adverbs. Friendly ends in -ly but is an adjective.
Advice, information and furniture are uncountable. Suggestion is countable: one suggestion, two suggestions.

B2.y: We do research, business and harm. But we make progress.
We make an effort, a profit and sense. But we do someone a favour.
We draw attention, a conclusion and a line. But we make a decision.
We reach a decision, an agreement and a conclusion. But we give a speech.
We raise a question, awareness and prices. But we pay or draw attention.
We run a business, a risk and a marathon. But we make a decision.
We commit a crime, fraud and an offence. But we do research.
We say highly likely, recommended and successful. But we say extremely tired.
We say deeply moved, concerned and rooted. But we say very expensive.
We say bitterly cold, disappointed and opposed. Bitterly goes with negative words, not happy.
Commence, purchase and assist are formal words. Grab is informal.
Kid, guy and mate are informal words. Gentleman is formal and polite.
Hang out, chill out and mess about are informal and relaxed. Deliberate means think carefully.
Crucial, vital and essential mean very important. Trivial means unimportant.
Obvious, evident and apparent mean easy to see. Obscure means hard to see or understand.
Cautious, wary and prudent mean careful. Reckless means not caring about danger.
Sufficient, adequate and ample mean enough. Scarce means not enough.
Obsolete, outdated and antiquated mean old-fashioned. Cutting-edge means very modern.
Furious, livid and enraged mean extremely angry. Irritated means only slightly annoyed.
Exhausted, drained and worn out mean very tired. Refreshed means full of energy again.
Anxious, uneasy and apprehensive mean worried. Serene means calm and peaceful.
Slim, slender and lean are positive ways to say thin. Scrawny is negative.
Confident, self-assured and assertive are positive. Arrogant is negative: too proud.
Thrifty, frugal and economical mean careful with money. Stingy is negative: unwilling to share.
Curious, inquisitive and interested are neutral or positive. Nosy is negative: too interested in others.
Determined, persistent and tenacious are positive. Stubborn is negative: refusing to change.
Revenue, turnover and income are money coming in. Expenditure is money going out.
Loan, mortgage and debt are money you owe. Savings are money you keep.
Resign, quit and step down mean leave a job. Hire means give someone a job.
Fire, sack and dismiss mean remove from a job. Promote means give a higher position.
Moreover, furthermore and in addition add a point. However introduces a contrast.
However, nevertheless and nonetheless show contrast. Therefore shows a result.
Therefore, consequently and thus show a result. Although shows contrast.
Put off, postpone and delay mean move to later. Bring forward means move earlier.
Call off, cancel and scrap mean stop a plan. Go ahead means it happens.
Come across, stumble upon and bump into mean find by chance. Look for means search.
Tolerate, endure and bear mean accept something unpleasant. Object to means protest.
Drizzle, shower and downpour are types of rain. Drought is a long time without rain.
Breeze, gale and gust are types of wind. Hail is frozen rain.
Grumble, moan and whinge mean complain. Praise means say good things.
Compliment, praise and applaud show approval. Criticise shows disapproval.
Inquire, query and question mean ask. Reply means answer.
Claim, state and assert mean say something is true. Deny means say it is not true.
Crash, bang and thud are loud, sudden noises. A whisper is soft and quiet.
Glow, sparkle and glitter describe light. Rumble describes a deep sound.
Drip, trickle and seep mean liquid flows slowly. Gush means it flows fast and strongly.
Nod, shrug and wink are body movements. Hum is a sound you make.
Frown, scowl and grimace show displeasure. Grin is a big smile.
Mutter, mumble and murmur mean speak quietly. Bellow means shout loudly.
Headline, article and editorial are found in newspapers. A sitcom is a TV comedy.

C1.y: We conduct research, an interview and an experiment. But we make a mistake.
Something can pose a threat, a question or a challenge. But we make an effort.
Terminate, conclude and cease mean end. Initiate means begin.
Alleviate, mitigate and ease mean make less severe. Intensify means make stronger.
Exacerbate, aggravate and worsen mean make worse. Alleviate means make better.
Hinder, impede and hamper mean make harder. Facilitate means make easier.
Verbose, long-winded and wordy mean using too many words. Concise means brief and clear.
Succinct, terse and pithy mean short and to the point. Rambling means long and unfocused.
Candid, frank and forthright mean speaking openly. Evasive means avoiding direct answers.
Ubiquitous, pervasive and omnipresent mean found everywhere. Scarce means hard to find.
Ephemeral, fleeting and transient mean lasting a short time. Enduring means lasting long.
Meticulous, scrupulous and painstaking mean very careful. Slapdash means careless and hurried.
Lethargic, sluggish and listless mean lacking energy. Vigorous means strong and energetic.
Benevolent, magnanimous and altruistic mean kind and generous. Malevolent means wanting to harm.
Renowned, acclaimed and eminent mean famous for good things. Notorious means famous for bad things.
Naive, gullible and credulous mean too easily fooled. Shrewd means clever and hard to fool.
Sceptical, dubious and wary mean doubting or not trusting. Trusting means believing easily.
Obstinate, intransigent and unyielding mean refusing to change. Compliant means willing to obey.
Laud, extol and commend mean praise. Disparage means speak badly of.
Reprimand, rebuke and admonish mean criticise formally. Commend means praise.
Clandestine, covert and surreptitious mean secret. Overt means done openly.
Melancholy, despondent and forlorn mean sad. Elated means extremely happy.
Garrulous, loquacious and voluble mean talking a lot. Taciturn means saying very little.
Destitute, impoverished and penniless mean very poor. Affluent means wealthy.
Belligerent, combative and pugnacious mean eager to fight. Conciliatory means trying to make peace.
Ambiguous, equivocal and cryptic mean unclear in meaning. Explicit means stated clearly.
Plethora, myriad and abundance mean a large amount. Dearth means a lack.
Dearth, paucity and scarcity mean too little. Surplus means more than needed.
Spurious, bogus and counterfeit mean false or fake. Authentic means genuine.
Composed, unflappable and level-headed mean calm under pressure. Flustered means confused and agitated.
Waver, vacillate and dither mean be unable to choose. Decide means make a choice.
Hoodwink, dupe and swindle mean trick someone. Level with means be honest with someone.
Irritable, cantankerous and testy mean easily annoyed. Genial means friendly and cheerful.
Obsequious, servile and sycophantic mean too eager to please. Defiant means openly resisting.
Rash, impetuous and foolhardy mean acting without thinking. Circumspect means cautious.
Mundane, humdrum and monotonous mean boring. Riveting means extremely interesting.
Intrepid, valiant and dauntless mean very brave. Craven means cowardly.
Ratify, endorse and approve mean officially support. Veto means officially reject.
Abolish, repeal and revoke mean officially end a law. Enact means make it law.
Fragrant, aromatic and perfumed mean smelling pleasant. Fetid means smelling very bad.
Quiver, tremble and shudder mean shake. Saunter means walk in a relaxed way.
Indolent, slothful and idle mean lazy. Industrious means hard-working.
Ostentatious, flamboyant and showy mean designed to impress. Understated means modest and subtle.
Obedient, docile and submissive mean easily controlled. Unruly means hard to control.
Adept, proficient and deft mean skilful. Inept means clumsy and unskilled.
Haughty, condescending and supercilious mean acting superior. Humble means modest.
Imply, insinuate and allude mean suggest indirectly. Proclaim means announce openly.
We bear a resemblance, a grudge and the brunt. But we draw a conclusion.
We harbour a grudge, doubts and suspicions. But we make a profit.
Governments levy a tax, a fine or a charge. A reward is offered, not levied.
